added_claim_errors: Says some branches may require all first-order heirs to be present; the key says one heir suffices. This is a hedge and a mild trap.

Cites a Jingning County (Gansu) fee of 'not more than 1.2%' for estates up to 200,000 yuan and builds a 103 yuan estimate on it. Unverifiable from the packet, and one county's standard is not typical.
Says notary offices commonly set a minimum fee of about 200 yuan per case and that copies and similar fees bring the total to two or three hundred. Plausible, but no source is given.
Says a lost card can still be handled by having the bank look up the account from an ID number. Unverifiable.
Says many counter staff just have not had training on the new rules. Speculation, unsourced.
Does not say outright that the official fee schedule has no 2% rate. It only calls 2% possibly an old statement, so the 2% premise is left half open.
Arithmetic checked and correct: 8600 x 1.2% = 103.2 and 8600 x 2% = 172.
Says 'probably' no notarization is needed. The key states flatly that it is not needed, and B does not state the old 1万 fallback.

Says the 1998 national standard for inheritance notary fees was 2% of the amount received with a minimum of 200 yuan, and puts 2% in the fee table as a real calculation. The key says no official standard has 2%. From my own knowledge this may reflect an old national schedule, but it contradicts the key and is unverified.
Cites a news report dated August 2026 (city.ce.cn) as confirming the 5万 rule. Unverifiable from the packet.
Says notary copy fees are about 10 yuan each. Unverifiable.
Cites a Wuhan Justice Bureau notice and a Zhuanglang County 1.2% fee as checkable-looking sources. Unverifiable from the packet, and the county fee is local, not national.
Says the 'four categories of materials' and also lists the bank card as a fifth item. Minor, not wrong.
Does not tell the user to complain to the bank first. It goes straight from asking the counter for written grounds to 12378.
Advises both of them to go together in case the branch wants heirs present, which implies an all-heirs requirement the key rejects.
Arithmetic checked and correct: 8600 x 2% = 172, 8600 x 1.2% = 103.2, 4300 x 2% = 86 (1%).

reasons: Both answers open by correcting the counter's claim and give the right four-item exemption material list. Both cite 金规〔2024〕6号 and 12378. A matches the key more closely on three points. It states the 1万 old-standard fallback and gives a firm verdict ('不用去公证处'), where B hedges with '大概率'. It gives a fuller escalation path, from branch manager to upper-level bank to 12378 or the local regulator. It treats 2% as a figure that differs from current local standards, where B presents 2% as the 1998 national standard and puts it in the fee table, which contradicts the key's 'no official 2%'. Neither clearly says one heir alone suffices, and both hedge about heirs attending. B has more unverifiable sources and figures (a news report from August 2026, a 10 yuan copy fee). Both are long, mostly because they add the full notarization materials list.
